blocks.content: The State shall take steps to organise village panchayats and endow them with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as units of self-government.

rows: Based on Gandhi's vision of rural self-reliance, decentralization, and moral self-rule.
Based on the ideology of democratic socialism aiming to establish a welfare state.
Promotion of village panchayats, cottage industries, co-operatives, and moral prohibition.
Reduction of income inequalities, securing livelihoods, equal pay, and distribution of material resources.

items: Article 40 (Organisation of Village Panchayats) was given practical shape through the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
Article 43B was added to the Gandhian DPSPs by the 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.
Questions frequently test identification of Gandhian principles versus Socialistic and Liberal-Intellectual principles in Part IV.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Gandhian principles represent the program of national reconstruction enunciated by Mahatma Gandhi during the freedom movement.
These principles are embodied within the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in Part IV of the Constitution.
Article 40 directs the State to organize village panchayats and endow them with authority to function as units of self-government.
Article 43 and 43B promote cottage industries and the voluntary formation and autonomous functioning of co-operative societies.
Articles 46, 47, and 48 focus on promoting educational/economic interests of SCs, STs, prohibition of intoxicating drinks, and prohibiting the slaughter of cows and calves.
